_comment: Dramatic sequences (milestone 9): dialogues that Plato's own text links in time or by an agreement to meet again. Each step quotes Burnet's Greek at the section that makes the link (checked by tools/structure.py against the library's text), and 'testimony' quotes an ancient or modern reader who groups the dialogues so. 'says' is the Workshop's one-line summary of the quoted words; the quotation is the evidence.

sequences.label: The trial and death of Socrates

testimony.quote: the Euthyphron, as: in it the charge against Socrates is brought forward; the Apology, since it was necessary for him to defend himself; the Crito, on account of his staying in prison; and afterwards the Phedon, since in it Socrates meets with the end of life
as the fourth, (where) the Theztetus, Euthyphron, (and) Apology; as the fifth, (where) the Criton, Phzedon, (and) Epistles

steps.says: Socrates leaves to answer Meletus' indictment at the King's Porch.

evidence.quote: εἰς τὴν τοῦ βασιλέως στοὰν ἐπὶ τὴν Μελήτου γραφὴν

steps.says: Euthyphro meets Socrates at the King's Porch, where the indictment is to be heard.

evidence.quote: ὀνομάζουσι μέντοι αὐτόν, ὡς ἐγᾦμαι, Μέλητον

steps.says: Socrates answers at his trial the indictment Meletus brought.

evidence.quote: Μέλητός με ἐγράψατο τὴν γραφὴν ταύτην

steps.says: In prison, Crito brings word that the ship from Delos is coming.
Phaedo tells why Socrates died long after the trial: the ship sent to Delos.

evidence.quote: τοῦ πλοίου ὃ εἰς Δῆλον Ἀθηναῖοι πέμπουσιν

testimony.quote: as the second, (where) the Sophist, Statesman

steps.says: Socrates asks Theodorus to meet him there again in the morning.

evidence.quote: ἕωθεν δέ, ὦ Θεόδωρε, δεῦρο πάλιν ἀπαντῶμεν

steps.says: Theodorus comes 'by yesterday's agreement', bringing the Stranger from Elea.
Socrates thanks Theodorus for Theaetetus and the Stranger; the statesman and the philosopher are still to come.

evidence.quote: ἐπειδὰν τόν τε πολιτικὸν ἀπεργάσωνταί σοι καὶ τὸν φιλόσοφον

testimony.quote: the one in which the Republic, Timzus, (and) Critias take the lead

steps.says: Socrates counts his guests of yesterday, his hosts today.

evidence.quote: τῶν χθὲς μὲν δαιτυμόνων, τὰ νῦν δὲ ἑστιατόρων

steps.says: Yesterday's talk was about the best constitution, which he then sums up.

evidence.quote: χθές που τῶν ὑπʼ ἐμοῦ ῥηθέντων λόγων περὶ πολιτείας ἦν τὸ κεφάλαιον

steps.says: Timaeus hands the next speech to Critias, as agreed.

evidence.quote: παραδίδομεν κατὰ τὰς ὁμολογίας Κριτίᾳ τὸν ἑξῆς λόγον

steps.says: Hermocrates is to speak third, after Critias.
The three of the Laws, Clinias, the Stranger and Megillus, meet again as agreed.

evidence.quote: πρὸς μὲν τὸ τῆς ὁμολογίας ἥκομεν ἅπαντες ὀρθῶς, ὦ ξένε, τρεῖς ὄντες, ἐγὼ καὶ σὺ καὶ Μέγιλλος ὅδε
